place.zh: 苏门答腊北端 · 班达亚齐

background.zh: 马六甲海峡是印度洋与南海之间的香料与胡椒通道。13—15世纪伊斯兰教沿商路传入苏门答腊北端，为亚齐的兴起提供了宗教与商业网络。
background.en: The Malacca Strait was the spice and pepper corridor between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea. Islam spread along the trade routes to northern Sumatra in the 13th–15th centuries, providing the religious and commercial networks behind Aceh's rise.

course.zh: 阿里·穆加亚特·沙建立亚齐苏丹国，控制苏门答腊北端的胡椒产地与港口。1511年葡萄牙攻占马六甲后，许多穆斯林商人转往亚齐，亚齐遂成为海峡西口的主要伊斯兰商港；17世纪伊斯坎达尔·穆达时期达到鼎盛。
course.en: Ali Mughayat Syah founded the sultanate and controlled the pepper-growing hinterland and ports of northern Sumatra. After Portugal took Malacca in 1511, many Muslim merchants shifted to Aceh, which became the leading Islamic port at the western mouth of the strait and peaked under Iskandar Muda in the 17th century.

outcome.zh: 亚齐长期保持独立，直到19世纪亚齐战争后被荷兰征服。其伊斯兰学术传统、港口贸易与抗荷记忆深刻塑造了今日亚齐的地方认同；印尼现给予亚齐特别自治地位。
outcome.en: Aceh remained independent until the Dutch conquest after the Aceh War of the 19th century. Its Islamic scholarship, port trade and memory of resistance shaped modern Acehnese identity; Indonesia now grants Aceh special autonomy.

background.zh: 冷战太空竞赛中，苏联率先发射卫星与载人飞船。肯尼迪1961年提出在十年内将美国人送上月球，阿波罗计划投入巨大资源。
background.en: In the Cold War space race the Soviet Union led with satellites and human spaceflight. Kennedy’s 1961 goal of landing an American on the Moon within a decade mobilised the Apollo programme.

course.zh: 1969年7月20日，阿姆斯特朗与奥尔德林乘“鹰”号登月舱降落静海，阿姆斯特朗成为第一个踏上月球的人；柯林斯留在指令舱。
course.en: On 20 July 1969 Armstrong and Aldrin landed the Eagle in the Sea of Tranquility; Armstrong became the first person on the Moon while Collins remained in orbit.

outcome.zh: 阿波罗11号实现了人类首次载人登月，展示了航天与系统工程能力，也成为冷战科技竞争的象征。
outcome.en: Apollo 11 achieved the first crewed Moon landing, demonstrating spaceflight and systems-engineering capability and becoming a symbol of Cold War technological competition.

summary.zh: 克利斯提尼在前508/507年重组雅典公民体，以地域部落取代血缘部落，扩大公民大会与五百人议事会，奠定雅典民主制度的基础。
summary.en: Cleisthenes reorganized the Athenian citizen body in 508/507 BCE, replacing kinship tribes with territorial ones and strengthening the Assembly and Council of Five Hundred, laying the foundations of Athenian democracy.

background.zh: 此前雅典由贵族寡头与僭主轮流统治。梭伦改革缓解债务危机，但未解决政治权力分配；庇西特拉图家族的僭主统治结束后，贵族派系再度争斗。
background.en: Athens had alternated between aristocratic oligarchy and tyranny. Solon's reforms eased debt but did not redistribute political power, and after the Peisistratid tyranny aristocratic factions contended again.

course.zh: 克利斯提尼把阿提卡划分为城市、海岸与内陆三区，混合组成十个新部落，以打破地方家族势力。他扩大五百人议事会，实行抽签与轮值，并引入陶片放逐法。
course.en: Cleisthenes divided Attica into city, coast and inland zones and mixed them into ten new tribes to break local clan power. He enlarged the Council of Five Hundred, used sortition and rotation, and introduced ostracism.

outcome.zh: 民主制度在波斯战争后进一步扩展，成年男性公民可直接参与立法、审判与军事决策；但妇女、外邦人与奴隶被排除在外。
outcome.en: Democracy expanded after the Persian Wars: adult male citizens could participate directly in lawmaking, courts and military decisions, while women, foreigners and slaves were excluded.

why.zh: 雅典民主是直接民主的经典样本，也是“谁属于政治共同体”这一排他性问题的经典样本。
why.en: Athenian democracy is the classic model of direct democracy and equally the classic case of exclusion from the political community.

sources.label: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Acropolis, Athens

background.zh: 奥斯维辛是纳粹德国最大的集中营与灭绝营，约110万人在这里遇害，其中绝大多数是犹太人。
background.en: Auschwitz was the largest Nazi concentration and extermination camp; about 1.1 million people were murdered there, the vast majority Jews.

course.zh: 1945年1月27日，苏联红军进入奥斯维辛，发现幸存者、尸体与大量遗留物。纳粹在此之前已疏散部分囚犯进行“死亡行军”。
course.en: On 27 January 1945 Soviet troops entered Auschwitz and found survivors, corpses and vast stores of belongings. The Nazis had evacuated many prisoners on death marches.

outcome.zh: 奥斯维辛解放成为大屠杀记忆的核心象征；1月27日被定为国际大屠杀纪念日。它提醒人们工业化的种族灭绝如何发生。
outcome.en: The liberation became a central symbol of Holocaust memory; 27 January is International Holocaust Remembrance Day. It stands as a warning of how industrialised genocide can occur.

summary.zh: 阿拔斯哈里发曼苏尔在底格里斯河畔建立“和平之城”巴格达，作为帝国首都。圆形城市与运河网络使其成为中世纪世界最大的商业与学术中心之一。
summary.en: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur founded Baghdad, the 'City of Peace', on the Tigris as the imperial capital. Its round plan and canal network made it one of the medieval world's greatest commercial and scholarly centres.

background.zh: 阿拔斯革命推翻倭马亚王朝后，需要一个新的首都，既靠近波斯与呼罗珊的支持基础，又能控制两河流域的农业与贸易。
background.en: After overthrowing the Umayyads, the Abbasids needed a new capital close to their Persian and Khurasani support base and able to control Mesopotamian agriculture and trade.

course.zh: 762年曼苏尔选定底格里斯河西岸的村落巴格达，规划圆形城墙、宫殿、清真寺与市场。城市通过运河连接幼发拉底河与底格里斯河，并吸引波斯、阿拉伯、犹太与基督教商人。
course.en: In 762 al-Mansur chose the village of Baghdad on the west bank of the Tigris and laid out a round walled city with palace, mosque and markets. Canals linked the Euphrates and Tigris, attracting Persian, Arab, Jewish and Christian merchants.

outcome.zh: 巴格达在8–9世纪达到鼎盛，智慧宫翻译运动汇集希腊、波斯与印度知识。1258年蒙古攻陷后城市衰落，但仍是区域中心。
outcome.en: Baghdad flourished in the eighth and ninth centuries, when the House of Wisdom translation movement gathered Greek, Persian and Indian knowledge. It declined after the Mongol sack of 1258 but remained a regional centre.

why.zh: 巴格达建城说明首都选址如何同时服务于政治合法性、农业税收与跨区域贸易；它也是伊斯兰黄金时代的物质基础。
why.en: Baghdad's founding shows how a capital's site serves political legitimacy, agricultural revenue and transregional trade at once; it was the material base of the Islamic Golden Age.

summary.zh: 苏莱曼一世在莫哈奇全歼匈牙利军队，国王路易二世阵亡。匈牙利作为统一王国解体，中欧进入奥斯曼与哈布斯堡长期争夺的时代。
summary.en: Suleiman I destroyed the Hungarian army at Mohács and King Louis II died. Hungary's unified kingdom broke up, and Central Europe entered a long Ottoman–Habsburg contest.

background.zh: 苏莱曼1521年夺取贝尔格莱德，随后以匈牙利为进攻维也纳的通道。匈牙利贵族分裂、援军不足，欧洲其他基督教国家也未能形成有效联盟。
background.en: Suleiman took Belgrade in 1521 and used Hungary as the corridor toward Vienna. The Hungarian nobility was divided, reinforcements were lacking, and other Christian powers failed to form an effective alliance.

course.zh: 1526年8月29日，匈牙利重装骑士在沼泽地形上向奥斯曼阵线冲锋，被轻骑兵与炮兵侧击包围。战斗持续约两小时，匈牙利军队几乎全军覆没。
course.en: On 29 August 1526 Hungarian heavy cavalry charged the Ottoman line across marshy ground and were enveloped by light cavalry and artillery. The battle lasted about two hours and the Hungarian army was almost annihilated.

outcome.zh: 苏莱曼进入布达后撤军，匈牙利分裂为哈布斯堡控制的西部、奥斯曼直辖的中部与特兰西瓦尼亚公国。三国格局延续一个半世纪。
outcome.en: Suleiman entered Buda and withdrew, leaving Hungary divided between a Habsburg west, an Ottoman centre and the principality of Transylvania. This three-part structure lasted a century and a half.

why.zh: 莫哈奇说明骑兵时代的战术在火炮与轻骑兵面前已经失效，也展示了王朝联姻与贵族分裂如何让一个国家在一天内失去独立。
why.en: Mohács shows the obsolescence of heavy-cavalry tactics before artillery and light cavalry, and how dynastic division and noble factionalism could cost a kingdom its independence in a single day.

summary.zh: 克莱武率东印度公司军队在普拉西击败孟加拉纳瓦布，靠阴谋与倒戈获胜。此役常被视为英国在印度建立统治的起点。
summary.en: Clive's East India Company force defeated the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey, winning through conspiracy and defection. The battle is often taken as the starting point of British rule in India.

background.zh: 1756年西拉杰·乌德·达乌拉攻占加尔各答的英国商馆，引发公司报复。克莱武重夺加尔各答后，与纳瓦布部将米尔·贾法尔及银行家秘密约定推翻纳瓦布。
background.en: In 1756 Siraj-ud-Daulah seized the British factory at Calcutta, provoking Company retaliation. After retaking Calcutta, Clive conspired with the Nawab's commander Mir Jafar and Bengali bankers to overthrow him.

course.zh: 1757年6月23日，克莱武约3000人对阵纳瓦布约5万人。大雨淋湿纳瓦布炮兵火药后，公司军队火力占优；米尔·贾法尔按约按兵不动，纳瓦布军溃败。
course.en: On 23 June 1757 Clive's roughly 3,000 men faced the Nawab's army of about 50,000. Rain ruined the Nawab's artillery powder while Company fire remained effective; Mir Jafar held back as agreed and the Nawab's army collapsed.

outcome.zh: 米尔·贾法尔被立为纳瓦布，公司获得孟加拉税收与贸易特权。1764年布克萨尔战役后，公司进一步成为北印度的实际统治者。
outcome.en: Mir Jafar was installed as Nawab and the Company gained revenue and trade privileges in Bengal. After Buxar in 1764 it became the effective ruler of much of northern India.

why.zh: 普拉西说明帝国扩张并不只靠战场优势，金融、情报与本地精英的背叛同样关键；它也开启了公司统治与孟加拉大饥荒的链条。
why.en: Plassey shows that imperial expansion rested not only on battlefield superiority but on finance, intelligence and local elite betrayal; it also opened the chain to Company rule and the Bengal famine.

sources.label: National Army Museum (UK) — The Battle of Plassey

summary.zh: 七七事变后，中日两军在上海展开三个月血战。中国军队以巨大伤亡粉碎日军速胜企图，但最终撤退，上海于11月陷落。
summary.en: After the Marco Polo Bridge Incident, Chinese and Japanese forces fought for three months in Shanghai. China's army inflicted huge costs and denied Japan a quick victory, but withdrew and lost the city in November.

background.zh: 1937年8月9日虹桥机场事件后，蒋介石决定主动在上海开辟战场，把日军进攻方向由华北引向华东，并争取国际关注。
background.en: After the Hongqiao airfield incident on 9 August 1937, Chiang Kai-shek chose to open a front in Shanghai, shifting Japanese attention from north China to the east and seeking international attention.

course.zh: 8月13日战斗爆发，中国军队围攻日本海军陆战队据点。日军随后多次增兵并实施两栖登陆，双方在罗店、宝山、四行仓库等地反复争夺。中国军队装备与海空支援不足，伤亡惨重。
course.en: Fighting began on 13 August as Chinese troops attacked Japanese marine positions. Japan reinforced repeatedly and landed amphibiously; the two sides fought over Luodian, Baoshan and the Sihang Warehouse. Chinese forces lacked armour, air and naval support and suffered enormous losses.

outcome.zh: 中国军队于11月撤退，上海沦陷，随后南京于12月失守并发生大屠杀。淞沪会战打破了日本“三个月灭亡中国”的计划，也把战争推向长期化。
outcome.en: Chinese forces withdrew in November, Shanghai fell, and Nanjing was lost in December, followed by the Nanjing Massacre. The battle shattered Japan's plan for a three-month victory and turned the war into a protracted conflict.

why.zh: 淞沪会战是全面抗战初期最惨烈的战役之一：它证明中国可以承受巨大牺牲继续抵抗，也暴露了工业与海空力量差距的代价。
why.en: Shanghai was one of the bloodiest battles of the early war: it proved China could absorb enormous sacrifice and keep fighting, while exposing the cost of industrial and naval-air weakness.

background.zh: 1942年德军夏季攻势指向高加索油田与伏尔加河交通线，斯大林格勒成为关键目标。希特勒要求同时夺取城市与油田，德军兵力被拉长。
background.en: The German summer offensive of 1942 aimed at the Caucasus oilfields and the Volga artery, making Stalingrad a key target. Hitler demanded both the city and the oilfields, stretching German forces.

course.zh: 德军与轴心盟军攻入城市，双方在废墟中逐屋争夺。11月苏军发动“天王星”反攻，合围德国第6集团军；1943年2月保卢斯投降。
course.en: German and Axis forces fought street by street in the ruined city. In November Soviet forces launched Operation Uranus, encircling the German Sixth Army; Paulus surrendered in February 1943.

outcome.zh: 德国第6集团军覆灭，轴心国在东线转入战略防御。斯大林格勒与中途岛、阿拉曼一起被视为二战转折点。
outcome.en: The German Sixth Army was destroyed and the Axis went onto the strategic defensive in the East. Stalingrad, with Midway and El Alamein, is seen as a turning point of World War II.

sources.label: Imperial War Museums — What you need to know about the Battle of Stalingrad

summary.zh: 中国军队在台儿庄与日军展开巷战，经过反复争夺后取得抗战初期少见的重大胜利，粉碎了日军打通津浦线的计划。
summary.en: Chinese troops fought street by street at Taierzhuang and won one of the few major victories of the war's early phase, frustrating Japan's plan to open the Tianjin–Pukou railway.

background.zh: 日军1937年占领北平、上海、南京后，企图南北夹击徐州，打通津浦铁路。第五战区司令李宗仁在台儿庄一带集结兵力，准备迎击南下的日军第十师团。
background.en: After taking Beijing, Shanghai and Nanjing in 1937, Japan sought to converge on Xuzhou from north and south and open the Tianjin–Pukou railway. Fifth War Zone commander Li Zongren concentrated forces around Taierzhuang to meet the advancing Japanese 10th Division.

course.zh: 3月下旬日军攻入台儿庄，中国守军依托运河与街巷顽强抵抗。4月初中国军队完成合围并发动反攻，日军被迫撤退。战斗极为惨烈，城镇大部分被毁。
course.en: Japanese troops entered Taierzhuang in late March; Chinese defenders held on amid the canal and street network. In early April Chinese forces completed an encirclement and counterattacked, forcing a Japanese withdrawal. The town was largely destroyed.

outcome.zh: 中国方面宣称歼敌万余人，日军承认较大损失。台儿庄胜利鼓舞了全国士气，但徐州随后仍于5月失守，战争进入长期消耗阶段。
outcome.en: China claimed more than ten thousand Japanese dead; Japan acknowledged substantial losses. The victory boosted national morale, but Xuzhou still fell in May and the war settled into attrition.

why.zh: 台儿庄说明抗战并非一边倒的溃败：在具体战役中，地形、巷战与兵力集中可以抵消日军的装备优势。
why.en: Taierzhuang shows the war was not a one-sided collapse: in specific battles, terrain, urban combat and concentrated force could offset Japan's material advantages.

summary.zh: 日军沿长江与淮河多路进攻武汉，中国军队以百万兵力抵抗四个多月，最终主动撤离。武汉会战标志着抗战进入相持阶段。
summary.en: Japan advanced on Wuhan along the Yangtze and Huai rivers; Chinese forces resisted for over four months before withdrawing. The battle marked the war's shift into a stalemate.

background.zh: 南京失守后，国民政府迁至武汉，这里成为政治、军事与工业内迁的枢纽。日军希望通过攻占武汉迫使中国投降，打通长江中游。
background.en: After Nanjing fell, the Nationalist government moved to Wuhan, which became a hub for politics, command and relocated industry. Japan hoped that taking Wuhan would force China's surrender and open the middle Yangtze.

course.zh: 1938年6月起日军从安庆、九江、大别山多路推进。中国军队在田家镇、万家岭等地顽强阻击，并在花园口决堤以迟滞日军（造成严重水灾）。10月武汉三镇相继失守。
course.en: From June 1938 Japanese forces advanced from Anqing, Jiujiang and the Dabie Mountains. Chinese troops fought hard at Tianjiazhen and Wanjialing, and the Yellow River dikes were breached at Huayuankou to slow the advance, causing severe flooding. Wuhan's three towns fell in October.

outcome.zh: 中国军队保存了主力，政府迁往重庆。日军虽占领武汉，却未能迫使中国投降，战争进入长期相持；黄河决堤造成数十万人死亡与大规模流离。
outcome.en: China preserved its main forces and moved the government to Chongqing. Japan took Wuhan but failed to force surrender, and the war entered prolonged stalemate; the dike breach killed or displaced hundreds of thousands.

why.zh: 武汉会战说明抗战的战略逻辑：以空间换时间、保存有生力量；同时提醒人们，军事决策的代价往往由平民承担。
why.en: Wuhan illustrates the strategy of trading space for time and preserving fighting strength, while reminding us that the cost of military decisions often fell on civilians.

summary.zh: 丹麦裔俄国航海家白令率大北方远征队抵达阿拉斯加湾，确认北美与亚洲并不相连，并为俄国在阿拉斯加的毛皮贸易开辟道路。
summary.en: The Danish-born Russian navigator Vitus Bering reached the Gulf of Alaska with the Great Northern Expedition, confirming that Asia and North America were not joined and opening the way for Russian fur trade in Alaska.

background.zh: 彼得大帝希望测绘西伯利亚并确认亚洲与美洲是否相连。白令1728年已穿过后来以他命名的海峡，但未看到北美海岸。
background.en: Peter the Great wanted Siberia surveyed and the Asia–America connection settled. Bering had already passed the strait later named for him in 1728, but had not sighted the North American coast.

course.zh: 1741年6月，白令的圣彼得号与奇里科夫的圣保罗号从堪察加出发，被风暴吹散。白令于8月抵达阿拉斯加湾，考察阿留申群岛部分海岸，随后因坏血病在十一月于白令岛附近失事。
course.en: In June 1741 Bering's St Peter and Chirikov's St Paul left Kamchatka and were separated by storm. Bering reached the Gulf of Alaska in August and reconnoitred part of the Aleutians, but was wrecked near Bering Island in November, suffering from scurvy.

outcome.zh: 幸存者带回海獭毛皮样本，引发俄国对阿拉斯加与阿留申群岛的殖民扩张。白令本人于1741年12月死于白令岛。
outcome.en: Survivors brought back sea-otter pelts, triggering Russian colonial expansion into Alaska and the Aleutians. Bering died on Bering Island in December 1741.

why.zh: 白令航行完成了西伯利亚—北美地理连接的最后确认，也开启了俄国太平洋殖民与毛皮贸易的生态破坏。
why.en: Bering's voyage completed the geographical confirmation of the Siberia–North America link and began Russian Pacific colonization and the ecological damage of the fur trade.

summary.zh: 爪哇夏连特拉王朝在8至9世纪建造婆罗浮屠，以九层坛城式结构、数千幅浮雕与72座佛塔构成世界最大的佛教纪念建筑。
summary.en: Java's Shailendra dynasty built Borobudur between the eighth and ninth centuries: a nine-tiered mandala with thousands of reliefs and 72 stupas, the largest Buddhist monument in the world.

background.zh: 8世纪的爪哇处于印度化王国与海上贸易网络的交汇处，印度教的普兰巴南与佛教的婆罗浮屠并存，显示王室对不同宗教传统的赞助。
background.en: Eighth-century Java sat at the meeting point of Indianized kingdoms and maritime trade. Hindu Prambanan and Buddhist Borobudur coexisted, showing royal patronage across religious traditions.

course.zh: 建筑以灰色火山石砌成，底部方形、上部圆形，象征从欲望世界到无色界的修行阶次。回廊浮雕描绘佛本生故事与善财童子求法，朝圣者顺时针绕行约五公里。
course.en: Built of grey volcanic stone, it rises from a square base to circular terraces, symbolizing progress from the realm of desire to formlessness. Gallery reliefs depict Jataka tales and Sudhana's quest; pilgrims walk some five kilometres clockwise.

outcome.zh: 婆罗浮屠在约1000年后被火山灰掩埋，1814年由莱佛士重新发现，20世纪完成大规模修复，1991年列入世界遗产，是印尼最重要的文化地标之一。
outcome.en: Buried under volcanic ash after about 1000, Borobudur was rediscovered by Raffles in 1814, extensively restored in the twentieth century and listed as a World Heritage Site in 1991. It is one of Indonesia's foremost cultural landmarks.

why.zh: 婆罗浮屠把佛教宇宙观转化为可步行的建筑路径，是东南亚海洋世界吸收印度宗教并再创造的代表作。
why.en: Borobudur turns Buddhist cosmology into a walkable architectural path — a masterpiece of Southeast Asia's maritime world absorbing and reworking Indian religions.

actors.zh: 佩德罗·阿尔瓦雷斯·卡布拉尔

summary.zh: 卡布拉尔率葡萄牙船队前往印度途中西偏，于1500年4月抵达巴西海岸，宣布该地属葡萄牙，巴西由此进入葡萄牙殖民体系。
summary.en: Sailing for India, Pedro Álvares Cabral swung west and reached the Brazilian coast in April 1500, claiming it for Portugal and bringing Brazil into the Portuguese colonial system.

background.zh: 1494年《托德西利亚斯条约》在大西洋划出西葡势力分界，使南美东部落入葡萄牙一侧。达伽马首航印度后，葡萄牙急于建立固定航线与贸易据点。
background.en: The 1494 Treaty of Tordesillas divided the Atlantic between Spain and Portugal, placing eastern South America on the Portuguese side. After Gama's first voyage, Portugal rushed to secure the route and trading posts.

course.zh: 1500年3月卡布拉尔率13船离开里斯本，为避开几内亚湾无风带而向西航行，4月22日看到陆地，命名“真十字架之地”。他停留约十天，与图皮人接触后继续前往印度。
course.en: Cabral left Lisbon in March 1500 with thirteen ships, sailed west to avoid the Gulf of Guinea doldrums and sighted land on 22 April, naming it the Land of the True Cross. He stayed about ten days, met Tupi peoples and continued to India.

outcome.zh: 葡萄牙最初关注红木（pau-brasil）贸易，随后建立甘蔗种植园与殖民地。巴西成为大西洋奴隶贸易的最大接收地之一，原住民人口则因疾病与奴役急剧下降。
outcome.en: Portugal initially exploited brazilwood, then established sugar plantations and colonies. Brazil became one of the largest destinations of the Atlantic slave trade, while Indigenous populations collapsed under disease and enslavement.

why.zh: 卡布拉尔登陆常被称作“发现巴西”，但对图皮人而言这是殖民接触的开端；巴西的建立与大西洋奴隶制密不可分。
why.en: Cabral's landing is often called the 'discovery' of Brazil, but for Tupi peoples it began colonial contact; Brazil's founding was inseparable from Atlantic slavery.

summary.zh: 东汉宦官蔡伦以树皮、麻头、破布和渔网造纸，并向朝廷奏报，使廉价书写材料得以推广，深刻改变了知识传播。
summary.en: The Eastern Han eunuch Cai Lun made paper from bark, hemp, rags and fishing nets and reported it to the court, helping spread a cheap writing material that transformed the transmission of knowledge.

background.zh: 此前中国书写多用竹简、木牍与丝帛：前者笨重，后者昂贵。西汉已有早期纸张的考古发现，说明造纸并非一人凭空发明。
background.en: Before this, Chinese writing used bamboo and wooden slips, heavy for long texts, or silk, which was expensive. Earlier Western Han paper fragments show that papermaking was not invented from nothing by one person.

course.zh: 据《后汉书》记载，蔡伦于105年用树皮、麻头、敝布和鱼网捣浆抄纸，奏报皇帝后受到嘉奖，纸遂被称为“蔡侯纸”。工艺随后经中亚在8世纪前后传入伊斯兰世界。
course.en: According to the Book of the Later Han, in 105 CE Cai Lun pulped bark, hemp, rags and nets into sheets and reported the method to the emperor, who rewarded him; the product was called Marquis Cai paper. The craft later reached the Islamic world via Central Asia around the eighth century.

outcome.zh: 造纸术成为中国四大发明之一，经伊斯兰世界传入欧洲，降低了书籍成本，为印刷术与识字普及提供了物质基础。
outcome.en: Papermaking became one of China's canonical inventions; carried through the Islamic world to Europe, it lowered the cost of books and provided the material basis for printing and wider literacy.

why.zh: 蔡伦的意义不在“发明”二字，而在于把造纸变成可推广的官营工艺——技术史常由这种制度化改良推动。
why.en: Cai Lun's significance lies less in inventing paper than in turning papermaking into a reproducible, court-sponsored craft — a pattern common in the history of technology.

place.zh: 苏联乌克兰切尔诺贝利

background.zh: 切尔诺贝利核电站4号机组在进行安全测试时，操作与设计缺陷叠加。反应堆为RBMK型，存在正空泡系数等固有风险。
background.en: A safety test at Chernobyl Unit 4 combined operator error with design flaws. The RBMK reactor had inherent risks, including a positive void coefficient.

course.zh: 4月26日凌晨，功率骤升导致蒸汽爆炸与石墨火灾，大量放射性物质释放。苏联初期信息不透明，随后疏散周边居民并建造石棺。
course.en: In the early hours of 26 April a power surge caused a steam explosion and graphite fire, releasing large amounts of radioactivity. Initial Soviet information was opaque; nearby residents were evacuated and a sarcophagus built.

outcome.zh: 事故造成数十人急性死亡，长期健康与环境影响持续；它加速了苏联核能安全改革，也成为全球核安全与信息公开的转折点。
outcome.en: Dozens died acutely and long-term health and environmental effects persist. The accident accelerated Soviet nuclear-safety reform and became a turning point for global nuclear safety and transparency.

background.zh: 日本宣布投降后，中国战区分区受降。南京是侵华日军中国派遣军总司令部所在地，受降仪式具有象征意义。
background.en: After Japan's announcement, surrender ceremonies were held by theatre. Nanjing, headquarters of the Japanese China Expeditionary Army, was chosen for the main China Theater ceremony.

course.zh: 9月9日，中国战区最高统帅代表何应钦在南京接受日本中国派遣军总司令冈村宁次投降，日军代表在投降书上签字。
course.en: On 9 September, He Yingqin, representing the Chinese supreme command, accepted the surrender of General Okamura Yasuji's China Expeditionary Army in Nanjing; Japanese representatives signed the instrument.

outcome.zh: 中国战区大规模军事行动结束，日军开始缴械遣返。受降与接收过程复杂，成为战后中国政治与军事格局的重要节点。
outcome.en: Large-scale operations in the China Theater ended and Japanese forces began disarmament and repatriation. The surrender and takeover process became a key node in postwar Chinese politics and military affairs.

title.en: China's Victory in the War of Resistance

background.zh: 中国抗日战争始于1931年九一八事变，1937年七七事变后进入全民族抗战。中国战场长期牵制日本陆军主力，是二战东方主战场。
background.en: China's war of resistance began with the Mukden Incident in 1931 and became a full national war after the Marco Polo Bridge Incident in 1937. The China theatre tied down the bulk of the Japanese army and was the main eastern theatre of World War II.

course.zh: 1945年8月15日日本宣布投降后，中国战区受降仪式于9月9日在南京举行。9月3日被定为抗日战争胜利纪念日。
course.en: After Japan's 15 August announcement, the China Theater surrender ceremony was held in Nanjing on 9 September. 3 September is marked as the anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance.

outcome.zh: 中国以巨大牺牲赢得抗战胜利，收复东北、台湾等地，成为联合国安理会常任理事国。战争也深刻改变了中国政治格局。
outcome.en: China won at enormous cost, recovered Manchuria and Taiwan, and became a permanent member of the UN Security Council. The war also transformed China's political order.

sources.label: United Nations — China and the UN

summary.zh: 巴比伦国王汉谟拉比颁布的282条判例刻于黑色闪长岩石碑，是现存最完整的古代两河流域法典，体现“以眼还眼”式的等级化正义。
summary.en: The 282 case laws of Hammurabi, carved on a black diorite stela, form the most complete surviving Mesopotamian law collection and embody a graded, retaliation-based justice.

background.zh: 两河流域早有乌尔纳姆法典等先例。汉谟拉比统一巴比伦尼亚后，需要以统一法律整合多元城邦，并宣示王权受神授正义约束。
background.en: Mesopotamia already had earlier codes such as Ur-Nammu's. After unifying Babylonia, Hammurabi needed a common law to integrate diverse city-states and to present royal power as subject to divinely given justice.

course.zh: 石碑上部刻汉谟拉比从太阳神沙马什手中接受权标的浮雕，下部为282条判例，涵盖财产、契约、婚姻、继承、伤害与农业。条文按社会等级区别处罚。
course.en: The stela shows Hammurabi receiving the symbols of authority from the sun god Shamash above 282 case laws covering property, contracts, marriage, inheritance, injury and agriculture, with penalties graded by social class.

outcome.zh: 法典并非现代意义上的成文宪法，而是判例汇编与王权宣传的结合。石碑于1901年在苏萨被发现，现藏卢浮宫。
outcome.en: The code is not a modern constitution but a blend of case law and royal propaganda. The stela was found at Susa in 1901 and is now in the Louvre.

why.zh: 汉谟拉比法典让我们看到法律如何同时承担治理、等级秩序与王权合法化的功能。
why.en: Hammurabi's code shows how law simultaneously served governance, social hierarchy and royal legitimation.

background.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫的改革与“新思维”放松了政治控制，经济困难与民族运动加剧。1991年八一九政变失败后，联盟权威迅速瓦解。
background.en: Gorbachev’s reforms and “new thinking” loosened political control while economic hardship and nationalist movements grew. After the failed August 1991 coup, the union’s authority collapsed.

course.zh: 1991年12月，俄罗斯、乌克兰、白俄罗斯领导人宣布成立独联体；12月26日苏联最高苏维埃通过决议，苏联停止存在。
course.en: In December 1991 the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus announced the Commonwealth of Independent States; on 26 December the Soviet parliament declared the USSR dissolved.

outcome.zh: 冷战两极格局终结，15个加盟共和国独立；俄罗斯继承苏联核武器与联合国席位，东欧与全球秩序重新调整。
outcome.en: The bipolar Cold War order ended and fifteen republics became independent; Russia inherited the Soviet nuclear arsenal and UN seat, reshaping Eastern Europe and the global order.

sources.label: Britannica — collapse of the Soviet Union
Wikipedia — Dissolution of the Soviet Union

summary.zh: 哥伦布在西班牙王室资助下横渡大西洋，于1492年抵达加勒比海岛屿，开启欧洲与美洲的持续接触，也带来殖民、疾病与人口灾难。
summary.en: Sponsored by the Spanish crown, Columbus crossed the Atlantic and reached the Caribbean in 1492, opening sustained European contact with the Americas — and with it colonization, disease and demographic catastrophe.

background.zh: 15世纪末，伊比利亚半岛完成收复失地运动，卡斯蒂利亚与阿拉贡联合，急需绕过葡萄牙寻找通往亚洲的航路。哥伦布相信向西航行可缩短到达东方的距离。
background.en: At the end of the fifteenth century, after the Reconquista and the union of Castile and Aragon, Spain sought a route to Asia that bypassed Portugal. Columbus believed sailing west would shorten the distance to the East.

course.zh: 1492年8月，哥伦布率圣玛丽亚号、平塔号与尼尼亚号从帕洛斯出海，10月12日抵达巴哈马群岛，随后到达古巴与伊斯帕尼奥拉岛。他始终认为自己到达的是亚洲边缘。
course.en: Columbus left Palos in August 1492 with the Santa María, Pinta and Niña, reached the Bahamas on 12 October, then Cuba and Hispaniola. He maintained to the end that he had reached the edge of Asia.

outcome.zh: 欧洲随后建立殖民地，哥伦布大交换带来作物、牲畜、白银与疾病。泰诺人口在数十年内急剧崩溃，跨大西洋奴隶贸易也随之扩张。
outcome.en: European colonies followed, and the Columbian exchange carried crops, livestock, silver and disease. The Taíno population collapsed within decades, and the transatlantic slave trade expanded.

why.zh: 1492年不是“发现”一个无人之地，而是两个长期隔绝的世界被强行连接；其后果同时包括全球化的开端与殖民暴力的开端。
why.en: 1492 did not 'discover' an empty land but forcibly connected two long-separated worlds; its consequences include both the beginnings of globalization and of colonial violence.

sources.label: Library of Congress — 1492: An Ongoing Voyage

summary.zh: 库克率奋进号抵达塔希提观测金星凌日，随后在波利尼西亚导航者图帕伊亚帮助下测绘南太平洋，开启英国对太平洋的系统探索。
summary.en: Cook reached Tahiti aboard the Endeavour to observe the transit of Venus, then, aided by the Polynesian navigator Tupaia, charted the South Pacific, opening systematic British exploration of the region.

background.zh: 18世纪欧洲天文学界希望通过全球观测金星凌日来测量日地距离。英国皇家学会与海军合作，把科学观测与寻找南方大陆的任务结合。
background.en: Eighteenth-century astronomers hoped to measure the Earth–Sun distance by observing the transit of Venus worldwide. The Royal Society and the Navy combined the observation with a search for the southern continent.

course.zh: 1769年4月，奋进号抵达塔希提，6月3日完成观测。库克随后环行新西兰并测绘东海岸，又抵达澳大利亚东岸。塔希提人图帕伊亚随船同行，提供岛屿方位与航海知识。
course.en: The Endeavour reached Tahiti in April 1769 and observed the transit on 3 June. Cook then circumnavigated New Zealand, charted its east coast and reached eastern Australia. Tupaia, a Tahitian navigator, joined the ship and supplied knowledge of islands and routes.

outcome.zh: 库克的测绘为英国后续殖民与海图制作奠定基础，也带来疾病、土地剥夺与文化冲击。图帕伊亚的作用长期被欧洲叙事忽略。
outcome.en: Cook's charts prepared the ground for British colonization and hydrography, while also bringing disease, land dispossession and cultural shock. Tupaia's role was long neglected in European accounts.

why.zh: 库克航行既是科学远征，也是帝国测绘；把它只讲成“发现太平洋”会抹去波利尼西亚人已有的航海知识。
why.en: Cook's voyage was both a scientific expedition and imperial surveying; telling it only as the 'discovery' of the Pacific erases the Polynesian navigational knowledge already there.

sources.label: Wikipedia — First voyage of James Cook

background.zh: 2019年底中国武汉出现新型冠状病毒肺炎病例，病毒随后跨越国界传播。2020年1月30日，世卫组织宣布“国际关注的突发公共卫生事件”，3月宣布全球大流行。
background.en: Cases of a novel coronavirus pneumonia appeared in Wuhan, China, in late 2019 and spread across borders. The WHO declared a public health emergency of international concern on 30 January 2020 and a pandemic in March.

course.zh: 各国采取封锁、旅行限制、社交距离与疫苗接种等措施。病毒持续变异，医疗系统承压，全球经济与供应链受到严重冲击。
course.en: Countries imposed lockdowns, travel restrictions, social distancing and vaccination campaigns. The virus kept mutating, health systems were strained, and the global economy and supply chains were hit hard.

outcome.zh: 疫情造成数百万人死亡，加速远程办公、数字经济与公共卫生体系建设，也加剧了国家间的不平等与政治争论。
outcome.en: The pandemic killed millions, accelerated remote work, the digital economy and public-health investment, and deepened inequalities and political disputes between states.

background.zh: 1944年盟军准备在西欧开辟第二战场。艾森豪威尔指挥“霸王行动”，选择诺曼底海滩登陆，以分散德军防御并建立滩头阵地。
background.en: In 1944 the Allies prepared a second front in Western Europe. Eisenhower commanded Operation Overlord, choosing the Normandy beaches to spread German defences and establish a bridgehead.

course.zh: 6月6日，盟军在五个海滩登陆，空降部队在侧翼着陆。奥马哈海滩伤亡惨重，但盟军逐步建立滩头阵地，随后突破诺曼底并解放巴黎。
course.en: On 6 June Allied forces landed on five beaches with airborne troops on the flanks. Omaha Beach was costly, but the Allies established a bridgehead, broke out of Normandy and liberated Paris.

outcome.zh: 诺曼底登陆开辟了欧洲第二战场，加速纳粹德国的崩溃。它也是历史上规模最大的两栖登陆行动之一。
outcome.en: D-Day opened the Western Front, accelerating the collapse of Nazi Germany. It remains one of the largest amphibious operations in history.

background.zh: 七年战争后英国加强殖民地征税与管控，殖民地以“无代表不纳税”反对。1775年列克星敦枪声后冲突扩大。
background.en: After the Seven Years' War Britain tightened taxation and control of the colonies, which resisted under “no taxation without representation”. Fighting widened after Lexington in 1775.

course.zh: 1776年7月4日，大陆会议通过杰斐逊起草的《独立宣言》，以自然权利与人民主权论证脱离英国的正当性。
course.en: On 4 July 1776 the Continental Congress adopted Jefferson's Declaration of Independence, justifying separation through natural rights and popular sovereignty.

outcome.zh: 宣言成为美国建国文本，也影响法国大革命、海地革命和后续反殖民运动；其“人人生而平等”与现实中的奴隶制形成长期矛盾。
outcome.en: The Declaration became a founding text of the United States and influenced the French and Haitian revolutions and later anti-colonial movements; its claim of equality coexisted with slavery.

sources.label: U.S. National Archives — Declaration of Independence

background.zh: 1939年德国入侵波兰引发欧洲战争，1941年珍珠港事件后战争扩展为全球冲突。1945年5月德国投降，日本仍在太平洋继续作战。
background.en: Germany's invasion of Poland in 1939 began the European war; Pearl Harbor in 1941 widened it into a global conflict. Germany surrendered in May 1945, while Japan fought on in the Pacific.

course.zh: 1945年8月，日本在核爆、苏联参战与盟军海空封锁下决定投降。9月2日签署投降书，各战区陆续举行受降仪式。
course.en: In August 1945, under atomic bombing, Soviet entry and Allied blockade, Japan decided to surrender. The instrument was signed on 2 September, followed by surrender ceremonies across the theatres.

outcome.zh: 战争造成约7000万至8500万人死亡，是历史上最惨烈的冲突。战后联合国成立，殖民体系加速瓦解，美苏两极格局形成。
outcome.en: The war killed an estimated 70–85 million people, the deadliest conflict in history. The United Nations was founded, colonial empires accelerated their retreat, and the US-Soviet bipolar order took shape.

summary.zh: 伊丽莎白一世授予东印度公司贸易特许状，公司从香料贸易起步，逐渐演变为拥有军队与领土的殖民政权。
summary.en: Elizabeth I granted the East India Company a trading charter; beginning with spices, the Company gradually became a colonial power with its own army and territory.

background.zh: 16世纪末，荷兰与葡萄牙已在亚洲建立贸易网络。英国商人希望绕过黎凡特中介，直接参与香料与纺织品贸易，遂请求王室授予垄断特许。
background.en: By the late sixteenth century the Dutch and Portuguese had built Asian trade networks. English merchants wanted to bypass Levantine intermediaries and trade directly in spices and textiles, and petitioned the crown for a monopoly charter.

course.zh: 1600年12月31日，公司获得对东印度贸易的15年垄断权。它在万丹、苏拉特等地设立商馆，17世纪后期以孟买、加尔各答和马德拉斯为中心扩张。1757年普拉西战役后取得孟加拉税收。
course.en: On 31 December 1600 the Company received a fifteen-year monopoly on trade to the East Indies. It established factories at Banten and Surat and expanded around Bombay, Calcutta and Madras; after Plassey in 1757 it acquired Bengal's revenue.

outcome.zh: 公司一度统治印度大片地区，拥有约20万军队。1857年印度起义后，英国政府于1858年接管印度，公司1874年正式解散。
outcome.en: The Company came to govern much of India and field an army of some 200,000. After the 1857 uprising the British government took over India in 1858, and the Company was formally dissolved in 1874.

why.zh: 东印度公司是“公司国家”的原型：商业特许、私人武装与领土统治结合，最终反过来迫使帝国政府接管。
why.en: The East India Company is the archetype of the corporate state: commercial charter, private army and territorial rule combined, until the imperial government was forced to take over.

summary.zh: 奥斯曼苏丹穆罕默德二世以重炮与海陆合围攻陷君士坦丁堡，延续千年的拜占庭帝国终结，奥斯曼帝国成为东南欧与东地中海的主导力量。
summary.en: Sultan Mehmed II took Constantinople with heavy cannon and a land-and-sea siege, ending the thousand-year Byzantine Empire and making the Ottomans the dominant power in southeastern Europe and the eastern Mediterranean.

background.zh: 拜占庭在第四次十字军后元气大伤，领土缩至君士坦丁堡及周边。穆罕默德二世在前任基础上修建鲁米利堡垒，控制博斯普鲁斯海峡，并雇佣匈牙利工匠铸造巨炮。
background.en: Byzantium never recovered from the Fourth Crusade and was reduced to Constantinople and its hinterland. Mehmed II built Rumeli Hisarı to control the Bosphorus and hired Hungarian founders to cast enormous cannon.

course.zh: 1453年4月6日起，奥斯曼军队炮击狄奥多西城墙；4月22日把战船经陆路拖入金角湾，完成合围。5月29日拂晓总攻，圣罗曼努斯门被突破，君士坦丁十一世战死。
course.en: Bombardment of the Theodosian walls began on 6 April 1453; on 22 April ships were hauled overland into the Golden Horn, completing the encirclement. In the dawn assault of 29 May the Gate of St Romanus was breached and Constantine XI died fighting.

outcome.zh: 城市成为奥斯曼首都，圣索菲亚改为清真寺。拜占庭学者与手稿西流，常被视为文艺复兴的催化剂之一；奥斯曼则继续向巴尔干与中东扩张。
outcome.en: The city became the Ottoman capital and Hagia Sophia a mosque. Byzantine scholars and manuscripts moved west, often cited as a catalyst of the Renaissance, while the Ottomans expanded into the Balkans and the Middle East.

why.zh: 1453年常被当作中世纪结束的标志，但更重要的是它展示了火药火炮如何改变城墙、城市与帝国之间的关系。
why.en: 1453 is often treated as the end of the Middle Ages, but its deeper significance is how gunpowder artillery changed the relationship between walls, cities and empires.

sources.label: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Historic Areas of Istanbul

summary.zh: 斐迪南与伊莎贝拉攻陷格拉纳达，结束伊比利亚半岛最后一个穆斯林政权，也完成了“收复失地运动”的政治叙事。
summary.en: Ferdinand and Isabella captured Granada, ending the last Muslim polity in Iberia and completing the political narrative of the Reconquista.

background.zh: 奈斯尔王朝自1238年起以格拉纳达为都，凭借山地、外交与北非联系维持独立。15世纪卡斯蒂利亚与阿拉贡联姻后，半岛力量对比向基督教王国倾斜。
background.en: The Nasrid dynasty had ruled from Granada since 1238, surviving through mountain defences, diplomacy and North African links. After the union of Castile and Aragon in the fifteenth century, the balance shifted toward the Christian kingdoms.

course.zh: 1482年起卡斯蒂利亚军队逐步蚕食格拉纳达外围。1491年围城开始，城内饥荒与内斗加剧；布阿卜迪勒于1492年1月2日投降，交出阿尔罕布拉宫。
course.en: From 1482 Castilian forces steadily reduced Granada's hinterland. The siege began in 1491 amid famine and factional strife; Boabdil surrendered on 2 January 1492 and handed over the Alhambra.

outcome.zh: 投降协议最初允许穆斯林保留宗教与财产，但1499年后强制改宗与驱逐加剧。格拉纳达的陷落与同年哥伦布远航、驱逐犹太人一起，构成西班牙帝国形成的关键年份。
outcome.en: The surrender terms initially protected Muslim religion and property, but forced conversion and expulsion intensified after 1499. Granada's fall, together with Columbus's voyage and the expulsion of the Jews in the same year, marks a founding moment of the Spanish empire.

why.zh: 1492年不只是“完成统一”，也是宗教同质化、帝国扩张与记忆政治同时启动的年份。
why.en: 1492 was not simply the completion of unification but the simultaneous launch of religious homogenization, imperial expansion and memory politics.

sources.label: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Alhambra, Generalife and Albayzín

summary.zh: 科尔特斯联合特拉斯卡拉等反阿兹特克部族，围困特诺奇蒂特兰93天。城市陷落，阿兹特克帝国灭亡，新西班牙殖民地建立。
summary.en: Cortés allied with Tlaxcala and other peoples opposed to the Aztecs and besieged Tenochtitlan for 93 days. The city fell, the Aztec Empire ended and the colony of New Spain was founded.

background.zh: 1519年科尔特斯登陆墨西哥湾，利用阿兹特克贡赋体系下的地方不满，与特拉斯卡拉结盟。蒙特祖马二世最初将其视为客人，后将其扣为人质。
background.en: Cortés landed on the Gulf coast in 1519 and exploited discontent within the Aztec tribute system, allying with Tlaxcala. Montezuma II initially received him as a guest, then was taken hostage.

course.zh: 1520年“悲痛之夜”西班牙人被逐出城，随后天花在城内爆发。1521年科尔特斯以木帆船控制湖面，切断供水与补给，围城93天。城市在巷战、饥饿与疾病中陷落。
course.en: The Spanish were driven out on the Noche Triste in 1520, after which smallpox struck the city. In 1521 Cortés used brigantines to control the lake, cut water and supplies, and besieged the city for 93 days. Street fighting, hunger and disease brought it down.

outcome.zh: 科尔特斯在废墟上建立墨西哥城，新西班牙成为西班牙最重要的殖民地之一。阿兹特克人口在战争、疫病与强制劳动下急剧下降。
outcome.en: Cortés built Mexico City on the ruins, and New Spain became one of Spain's most important colonies. The Aztec population collapsed under war, epidemic disease and forced labour.

why.zh: 阿兹特克覆灭不是“少数人征服多数人”的简单故事，而是疫病、地方联盟、内政裂痕与武器差异共同作用的结果。
why.en: The Aztec defeat is not a simple story of few conquering many but the product of epidemic disease, local alliances, internal divisions and differences in weaponry.

sources.label: Wikipedia — Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire

background.zh: 东德经济停滞、改革压力与逃亡潮加剧。匈牙利开放边境后，大量东德人经奥地利逃往西德，抗议扩大。
background.en: East Germany faced economic stagnation, reform pressure and a refugee wave. After Hungary opened its border, many East Germans fled via Austria and protests grew.

course.zh: 1989年11月9日，东德政府误发放宽旅行限制的公告，民众涌向检查站，边防人员最终开放通道，柏林墙被跨越和拆除。
course.en: On 9 November 1989 a mistaken East German announcement eased travel restrictions; crowds surged to checkpoints, guards opened the barriers and the Wall was crossed and dismantled.

outcome.zh: 柏林墙倒塌成为冷战结束的象征，推动两德统一与东欧剧变；欧洲政治地图随之重绘。
outcome.en: The fall became a symbol of the end of the Cold War, accelerated German reunification and the 1989 revolutions, and redrew Europe's political map.

sources.label: Imperial War Museums — What was the Berlin Wall and how did it fall?

summary.zh: 东汉在黄巾起义、军阀割据与宫廷斗争中瓦解。220年汉献帝禅位于曹丕，汉朝结束，中国进入三国时代。
summary.en: The Eastern Han disintegrated amid the Yellow Turban revolt, warlordism and court intrigue. In 220 Emperor Xian abdicated to Cao Pi, ending the Han and opening the Three Kingdoms period.

background.zh: 东汉后期外戚与宦官交替专权，土地兼并加剧，地方豪强与州牧掌握军政。184年黄巾起义虽被镇压，却使地方军阀合法化。
background.en: In the later Eastern Han, consort families and eunuchs alternated in power, land concentration worsened, and provincial magnates gained military control. The Yellow Turban revolt of 184 was crushed but legitimized regional warlords.

course.zh: 董卓入京后废立皇帝，引发关东联军讨伐。曹操迎汉献帝至许昌，以“挟天子以令诸侯”统一北方。220年曹操死后，曹丕逼献帝禅让，建立魏国。
course.en: Dong Zhuo's seizure of the capital and deposition of the emperor triggered a coalition of eastern warlords. Cao Cao took Emperor Xian to Xuchang and unified the north under imperial cover. After Cao Cao's death in 220, Cao Pi forced the emperor's abdication and founded Wei.

outcome.zh: 刘备与孙权随后分别称帝，形成魏、蜀、吴三国。汉朝四百年的制度与正统观念并未消失，反而成为后世政权反复援引的政治资源。
outcome.en: Liu Bei and Sun Quan soon claimed imperial titles, forming Wei, Shu and Wu. The Han's four-century institutions and legitimacy did not disappear but became political resources later dynasties repeatedly invoked.

why.zh: 东汉灭亡说明一个王朝可以在名义上延续、实际上已被军阀掏空；禅让的形式则让权力转移披上了合法外衣。
why.en: The fall of the Han shows how a dynasty can survive in name while warlords hollow it out, and how abdication gave power transfer a legal form.

sources.label: Wikipedia — End of the Han dynasty
The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Han Dynasty (206 B.C.-220 A.D.)

summary.zh: 皮萨罗在卡哈马卡突袭并俘获印加皇帝阿塔瓦尔帕，随后处死他并占领库斯科；内战、天花与西班牙盟军共同导致印加帝国崩溃。
summary.en: Pizarro ambushed and captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa at Cajamarca, later executing him and occupying Cusco; civil war, smallpox and Spanish-allied forces together brought down the Inca Empire.

background.zh: 印加帝国以库斯科为中心，通过道路、驿站与米塔劳役制度统治安第斯山区。1520年代天花传入，杀死皇帝瓦伊纳·卡帕克并引发瓦斯卡与阿塔瓦尔帕的内战。
background.en: The Inca state, centred on Cusco, governed the Andes through roads, way stations and the mit'a labour system. Smallpox arrived in the 1520s, killing Emperor Huayna Capac and triggering civil war between Huáscar and Atahualpa.

course.zh: 1532年皮萨罗率约180人抵达卡哈马卡。阿塔瓦尔帕在广场被伏击俘获，虽支付巨额金银赎金仍于1533年被处死。西班牙人随后与反对库斯科的部族结盟，进入首都。
course.en: Pizarro reached Cajamarca in 1532 with about 180 men. Atahualpa was ambushed and captured in the square; despite a vast gold and silver ransom he was executed in 1533. The Spanish then allied with peoples opposed to Cusco and entered the capital.

outcome.zh: 西班牙建立总督区，利用原有道路与劳役制度统治安第斯。印加抵抗持续数十年，直到1572年比尔卡班巴陷落。人口因疾病、战争与强制劳动急剧下降。
outcome.en: Spain established a viceroyalty, ruling the Andes through existing roads and labour systems. Inca resistance continued for decades until Vilcabamba fell in 1572, while disease, war and forced labour devastated the population.

why.zh: 印加覆灭不是百余西班牙人击败百万人口帝国的神话，而是内战、疫病、地方联盟与火器共同作用的结果。
why.en: The fall of the Inca was not a mythic victory of a hundred Spaniards over a million-person empire, but the product of civil war, epidemic disease, local alliances and firearms.

sources.label: Wikipedia — Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire
UNESCO World Heritage Centre — City of Cuzco

title.en: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

summary.zh: 日耳曼将领奥多亚塞废黜末代西罗马皇帝罗慕路斯·奥古斯都，西罗马帝国灭亡。东部帝国延续为拜占庭，西欧进入诸王国并立的中世纪。
summary.en: The Germanic commander Odoacer deposed the last Western emperor, Romulus Augustulus, ending the Western Roman Empire. The Eastern Empire continued as Byzantium, while Western Europe entered a medieval world of successor kingdoms.

background.zh: 三世纪危机后，西罗马面临财政枯竭、军队蛮族化、内战与边境压力。410年罗马被西哥特人洗劫，西部政府逐渐失去对高卢、西班牙与北非的控制。
background.en: After the third-century crisis, the Western empire faced fiscal exhaustion, barbarization of the army, civil war and frontier pressure. Rome was sacked by the Visigoths in 410, and the western government gradually lost Gaul, Spain and North Africa.

course.zh: 476年，奥多亚塞率雇佣军废黜罗慕路斯·奥古斯都，把帝国徽记送往君士坦丁堡，名义上承认东部皇帝。他不称帝，而以“意大利国王”身份统治。
course.en: In 476 Odoacer's mercenaries deposed Romulus Augustulus and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople, nominally recognizing the eastern emperor. He did not claim the purple but ruled as king of Italy.

outcome.zh: 西罗马的制度、道路与教会结构并未一夜消失，而是在日耳曼王国、拜占庭与基督教教会之间重组。476年因此成为古代与中世纪分期的传统标志。
outcome.en: Western Roman institutions, roads and church structures did not vanish overnight but were reorganized among Germanic kingdoms, Byzantium and the Christian church. 476 therefore became the conventional dividing line between antiquity and the Middle Ages.

why.zh: “罗马灭亡”不是单一事件，而是长期转型；476年之所以重要，是因为它给一个漫长的过程提供了一个可讲述的终点。
why.en: The 'fall of Rome' was not a single event but a long transformation; 476 matters because it gave a long process a tellable ending.

sources.label: Britannica — Why did the Roman Empire fall?
Wikipedia — Fall of the Western Roman Empire
The Metropolitan Museum of Art — The Roman Empire (27 B.C.-393 A.D.)

summary.zh: 罗马人把建城追溯到前753年的罗慕路斯传说；考古则显示帕拉蒂尼山在公元前8世纪已出现聚落，罗马由此逐步成长为地中海帝国。
summary.en: Romans traced their city to Romulus in 753 BCE; archaeology shows settlements on the Palatine by the eighth century BCE, from which Rome grew into a Mediterranean empire.

background.zh: 罗马建城故事融合了阿尔巴隆伽王位斗争、双子被母狼哺育与兄弟相残的母题。它并非同时代记录，而是罗马人在数百年后对自身起源的整理。
background.en: The foundation story blends a dynastic struggle at Alba Longa, twins suckled by a she-wolf and fratricide. It is not a contemporary record but Rome's later shaping of its own origins.

course.zh: 传说罗慕路斯在帕拉蒂尼山划出城界，杀死越界的雷穆斯，并招纳逃亡者与萨宾妇女形成早期人口。王政时代随后延续约两个半世纪。
course.en: In the legend Romulus marked the city boundary on the Palatine, killed Remus for crossing it, and built an early population from fugitives and Sabine women. The regal period then lasted about two and a half centuries.

outcome.zh: 罗马以城邦制度、拉丁公民权与道路网络为基础不断扩张，最终在公元前3世纪统一意大利半岛，并在帝国时期统治地中海世界。
outcome.en: Built on city-state institutions, Latin citizenship and roads, Rome expanded to unify the Italian peninsula by the third century BCE and later ruled the Mediterranean as an empire.

why.zh: 罗马建城传说不仅解释城市起源，也为罗马的扩张、内战与帝国合法性提供了持续被重述的政治神话。
why.en: The foundation myth did more than explain the city: it supplied a political myth repeatedly retold to justify Rome's expansion, civil wars and imperial authority.

sources.label: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Historic Centre of Rome

background.zh: 18世纪法国财政危机、等级制度与启蒙思想传播，使旧制度合法性动摇。路易十六被迫召开三级会议，第三等级自行组成国民议会。
background.en: In eighteenth-century France fiscal crisis, the estate system and Enlightenment ideas undermined the ancien régime. Louis XVI convened the Estates-General; the Third Estate broke away to form a National Assembly.

course.zh: 1789年7月14日巴黎民众攻占巴士底狱，革命爆发。随后废除封建特权、发表《人权宣言》，建立君主立宪，1792年成立共和国，1793年处决路易十六，进入恐怖统治。
course.en: On 14 July 1789 Parisians stormed the Bastille. The revolution abolished feudal privilege, issued the Declaration of the Rights of Man, established a constitutional monarchy, then a republic in 1792; Louis XVI was executed in 1793 and the Terror followed.

outcome.zh: 革命传播了自由、平等、主权在民的理念，重塑法国与欧洲政治；它也带来战争、恐怖与拿破仑的崛起。
outcome.en: The revolution spread ideals of liberty, equality and popular sovereignty, transforming France and Europe; it also brought war, terror and Napoleon’s rise.

background.zh: 2011年3月11日，日本东北海域发生9.0级地震并引发海啸。福岛第一核电站的防波堤低于海啸高度。
background.en: On 11 March 2011 a magnitude 9.0 earthquake off Tōhoku generated a tsunami. The seawall at Fukushima Daiichi was lower than the wave.

course.zh: 海啸淹没应急电源，导致反应堆失去冷却并发生氢气爆炸与放射性释放。周边居民被疏散，事故等级最终定为7级。
course.en: The tsunami flooded emergency power, causing loss of cooling, hydrogen explosions and radioactive releases. Nearby residents were evacuated; the accident was rated Level 7.

outcome.zh: 事故推动日本核能政策与全球核安全标准反思，福岛重建与污染水处置长期争议。地震海啸本身造成近两万人死亡或失踪。
outcome.en: The accident forced a rethink of Japanese nuclear policy and global safety standards; reconstruction and treated-water disposal remain contested. The earthquake and tsunami killed or left missing nearly 20,000 people.

summary.zh: 铁木真在1206年统一蒙古诸部，被推举为成吉思汗，建立以千户制、怯薛军与札撒法为基础的帝国，随后展开横跨欧亚的征服。
summary.en: In 1206 Temüjin unified the Mongol tribes and was proclaimed Genghis Khan, founding an empire built on decimal units, the imperial guard and the Yasa, which then expanded across Eurasia.

background.zh: 12世纪的蒙古高原部族林立、互相劫掠。铁木真幼年丧父、历经俘掳与联盟背叛，逐步吸收克烈、乃蛮等部的力量。
background.en: Twelfth-century Mongolia was divided among raiding tribes. Temüjin lost his father as a child, survived captivity and shifting alliances, and gradually absorbed the Keraite, Naiman and other groups.

course.zh: 1206年的忽里台大会推举铁木真为成吉思汗。他打破血缘部落，按十户、百户、千户、万户编组民众，建立驿站（站赤）与统一法律，并以怯薛军控制贵族。
course.en: A kurultai in 1206 proclaimed Temüjin Genghis Khan. He broke up kinship tribes into units of ten, a hundred, a thousand and ten thousand, built the yam relay system and a common law, and used the imperial guard to control the aristocracy.

outcome.zh: 蒙古军队随后征服金朝北方、花剌子模与中亚，成吉思汗1227年去世时帝国已横跨蒙古、华北与中亚。其后继者建立元朝与诸汗国，形成欧亚交流的空前网络。
outcome.en: Mongol armies went on to conquer northern China, Khwarazm and Central Asia; at Genghis Khan's death in 1227 the empire stretched from Mongolia to Central Asia. His successors founded the Yuan dynasty and the khanates, creating an unprecedented network of Eurasian exchange.

why.zh: 成吉思汗的崛起说明草原政治可以通过制度化而非仅靠个人魅力整合；蒙古征服也同时带来破坏与跨大陆交流。
why.en: Genghis Khan's rise shows that steppe politics could be integrated by institutions, not charisma alone; the conquests brought both destruction and transcontinental exchange.

sources.label: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — The Legacy of Genghis Khan

summary.zh: 希腊人在1821年起义反抗奥斯曼统治，经历惨烈战争与列强干预，最终在1830年获得独立，成为近代第一个脱离奥斯曼帝国的欧洲民族国家。
summary.en: Greeks rose against Ottoman rule in 1821; after bitter fighting and great-power intervention they won independence in 1830, becoming the first modern European nation-state to break from the Ottoman Empire.

background.zh: 奥斯曼帝国境内的希腊人享有宗教自治，但缺乏政治权利。启蒙思想、法国大革命与希腊商业侨民的民族意识，为秘密组织“友谊社”提供了土壤。
background.en: Greeks within the Ottoman Empire had religious autonomy but few political rights. Enlightenment ideas, the French Revolution and the Greek commercial diaspora fed the nationalism of the secret Philikí Etaireía.

course.zh: 1821年3月起义在多处爆发。奥斯曼镇压极为残酷，1822年希俄斯岛大屠杀震动欧洲。1825年埃及军队在易卜拉欣帕夏率领下入侵，攻陷米索隆吉。1827年英法俄联合舰队在纳瓦里诺摧毁埃土舰队。
course.en: Revolts broke out in March 1821. Ottoman repression was severe, and the 1822 Chios massacre shocked Europe. In 1825 Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptian army invaded and took Missolonghi; in 1827 a joint British–French–Russian fleet destroyed the Ottoman–Egyptian fleet at Navarino.

outcome.zh: 1830年伦敦议定书承认希腊独立，1832年划定边界并迎立巴伐利亚的奥托为国王。独立战争成为欧洲浪漫主义与民族主义的标志性事件。
outcome.en: The 1830 London Protocol recognized Greek independence; borders were set in 1832 and Otto of Bavaria became king. The war became a landmark of European romantic nationalism.

why.zh: 希腊独立战争展示了民族主义、宗教认同与列强均势如何交织；它也暴露了“自由希腊”叙事对奥斯曼治下其他群体的遮蔽。
why.en: The war shows how nationalism, religious identity and great-power balance intertwined; it also exposes how the narrative of a 'free Greece' obscured other Ottoman communities.

background.zh: 15世纪欧洲纸张普及、金属工艺与葡萄酒压榨技术成熟，为活字印刷提供条件。古腾堡在美因茨试验金属活字与油墨。
background.en: In fifteenth-century Europe paper, metalworking and wine-press technology made movable type feasible. Gutenberg experimented with metal type and oil-based ink in Mainz.

course.zh: 古腾堡用铅合金活字、油墨和压榨机印刷《四十二行圣经》，约1455年完成。印刷术随后迅速传播到欧洲各地。
course.en: Gutenberg printed the 42-line Bible with lead-alloy type, oil ink and a press, completing it around 1455. Printing spread rapidly across Europe.

outcome.zh: 印刷术降低了书籍成本，加速宗教改革、科学革命与民族语言的形成，被视为知识传播的转折点。
outcome.en: Printing cut the cost of books and accelerated the Reformation, the Scientific Revolution and vernacular literature, becoming a turning point in the spread of knowledge.

summary.zh: 经历十余年战争，德萨林于1804年宣布海地独立，建立世界上第一个由被奴役者起义建立的国家，也是拉美第一个独立共和国。
summary.en: After more than a decade of war, Dessalines declared Haiti independent in 1804, founding the world's first state created by an uprising of enslaved people and the first independent republic in Latin America.

background.zh: 圣多明各是法国最富庶的殖民地，建立在残酷的甘蔗种植园奴隶制上。法国大革命的“自由平等”口号传入殖民地，激化了自由有色人种与奴隶的反抗。
background.en: Saint-Domingue was France's richest colony, built on brutal sugar-plantation slavery. The French Revolution's language of liberty and equality reached the colony and sharpened resistance among free people of colour and the enslaved.

course.zh: 1791年奴隶起义爆发，杜桑·卢维杜尔组织军队，先后对抗法国、西班牙与英国。1802年拿破仑派军恢复奴隶制，杜桑被俘；德萨林与克里斯托夫继续抵抗，1803年击败法军。
course.en: A slave uprising began in 1791; Toussaint Louverture built an army that fought France, Spain and Britain in turn. Napoleon sent an expedition to restore slavery in 1802 and Toussaint was captured; Dessalines and Christophe fought on and defeated the French in 1803.

outcome.zh: 1804年1月1日德萨林在戈纳伊夫宣读独立宣言，恢复阿拉瓦克语名称“海地”。法国随后索取巨额赔款，长期拖累海地经济；奴隶制列强也长期拒绝承认这个黑人共和国。
outcome.en: On 1 January 1804 Dessalines read the declaration of independence at Gonaïves, restoring the Arawak name Haiti. France later imposed a huge indemnity that burdened Haiti for generations, and slaveholding powers long refused to recognize the Black republic.

why.zh: 海地独立把奴隶制问题变成国际政治问题，证明被奴役者可以建立国家；其后的赔款与孤立则展示了“胜利之后的惩罚”。
why.en: Haitian independence made slavery an international political question and proved that the enslaved could found a state; the indemnity and isolation that followed show the 'punishment after victory'.

background.zh: 圣多明各是法国最富庶的糖岛，建立在残酷的奴隶制之上。法国大革命的“自由平等”口号传至殖民地，激化了自由有色人与奴隶的反抗。
background.en: Saint-Domingue was France's richest sugar colony, built on brutal slavery. The French Revolution's language of liberty reached the colony and sharpened resistance among free people of colour and the enslaved.

course.zh: 1791年奴隶起义爆发，杜桑·卢维杜尔等领袖组织军队，先后对抗法国、西班牙和英国。1802年拿破仑派军镇压，杜桑被捕。
course.en: A slave uprising began in 1791; leaders such as Toussaint Louverture built armies that fought France, Spain and Britain. Napoleon sent an expedition in 1802 and Toussaint was captured.

outcome.zh: 1804年海地宣布独立，成为第一个由被奴役者建立的黑人共和国。法国随后索取巨额赔款，长期拖累海地经济。
outcome.en: Haiti declared independence in 1804, becoming the first Black republic founded by formerly enslaved people. France later imposed a huge indemnity that burdened Haiti for generations.

background.zh: 美国曼哈顿计划研制出原子弹。为迫使日本投降、避免登陆日本本土的巨大伤亡，杜鲁门政府决定使用原子弹。7月26日的《波茨坦公告》遭日本“默杀”后，作战准备继续推进。
background.en: The Manhattan Project produced the atomic bomb. To force Japan's surrender and avoid the huge casualties of an invasion of the home islands, the Truman administration decided to use it. After Japan's 'mokusatsu' response to the Potsdam Declaration, preparations went ahead.

course.zh: 8月6日上午8时15分，B-29轰炸机“艾诺拉·盖伊”在广岛投下代号“小男孩”的铀弹，在离地约580米处爆炸。城市中心被毁，随后引发大火与辐射伤害。
course.en: At 8:15 a.m. on 6 August, the B-29 Enola Gay dropped the uranium bomb 'Little Boy' over Hiroshima; it detonated about 580 metres above the city. The centre was destroyed, followed by fire and radiation injury.

outcome.zh: 到1945年底，死亡人数估计约7万至14万，具体数字仍有争议。日本未立即投降；三天后长崎再遭核爆，苏联也对日宣战。
outcome.en: By the end of 1945 the death toll is estimated at roughly 70,000–140,000, with the exact figure debated. Japan did not surrender immediately; Nagasaki was bombed three days later and the Soviet Union declared war.

sources.label: U.S. National Archives — Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Britannica — Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

summary.zh: 八路军在华北对日军交通线与据点发动大规模破袭战，参战部队达百余团，是抗战中共产党军队最大规模的主动进攻。
summary.en: The Eighth Route Army launched a large-scale sabotage offensive against Japanese rail lines and strongpoints in north China, involving over a hundred regiments — the Communist forces' largest offensive of the war.

background.zh: 抗战进入相持阶段后，日军在华北推行“囚笼政策”，以铁路、公路与据点分割根据地。八路军希望以破袭战打破封锁并提振士气。
background.en: As the war stalemated, Japan's 'cage' policy in north China used railways, roads and strongpoints to divide Communist base areas. The Eighth Route Army sought to break the blockade and raise morale with a sabotage campaign.

course.zh: 1940年8月起，八路军集中百余团兵力破坏正太铁路、公路与桥梁，并攻击据点。日军随后调集兵力报复，对根据地实施“扫荡”，双方均付出重大代价。
course.en: From August 1940 more than a hundred regiments attacked the Zhengding–Taiyuan railway, roads and bridges, and assaulted strongpoints. Japan retaliated with sweeping operations against base areas; both sides paid heavily.

outcome.zh: 战役打破了日军的封锁，也暴露了八路军的力量，招致更残酷的报复与根据地困难。它成为中共抗战叙事中的重要象征。
outcome.en: The offensive disrupted the blockade but exposed the Eighth Route Army's strength, provoking harsher retaliation and hardship in the base areas. It became a central symbol in the CCP's narrative of the war.

why.zh: 百团大战展示了敌后战场的规模与代价；它也提醒我们，游击战与大规模进攻之间的转换会带来战略暴露。
why.en: The offensive shows the scale and cost of the behind-the-lines front, and how switching from guerrilla warfare to a large offensive can expose a movement strategically.

place.zh: 印度波克兰 / 巴基斯坦恰盖

background.zh: 印度在1974年进行过一次“和平核爆炸”，巴基斯坦则长期寻求对等能力。1996年《全面禁止核试验条约》开放签署，但印巴均未加入，南亚安全困境持续。
background.en: India conducted a 'peaceful nuclear explosion' in 1974, while Pakistan long sought a matching capability. The Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty opened for signature in 1996, but neither India nor Pakistan joined, and South Asia's security dilemma persisted.

course.zh: 1998年5月11日和13日，印度在波克兰进行多次地下核试验；5月28日，巴基斯坦在恰盖进行核试验作为回应。两国随后宣布具备核武器能力，国际社会实施制裁并推动对话。
course.en: On 11 and 13 May 1998 India conducted a series of underground tests at Pokhran; on 28 May Pakistan responded with tests at Chagai. Both declared nuclear-weapon capabilities, prompting sanctions and diplomatic engagement.

outcome.zh: 南亚进入公开核威慑时代。1999年《拉合尔宣言》短暂缓和局势，但1999年卡吉尔冲突与后续危机显示核威慑下的常规冲突风险仍在。核供应国集团对印巴实施出口限制，地区核治理至今是国际安全的核心议题。
outcome.en: South Asia entered an era of open nuclear deterrence. The 1999 Lahore Declaration briefly eased tensions, but the Kargil conflict and later crises showed that conventional conflict remains possible under nuclear deterrence. Nuclear Suppliers Group restrictions and regional nuclear governance remain central security issues.

background.zh: 苏门答腊岛西北海域发生巨型逆冲地震，震级约9.1—9.3，引发跨越印度洋的海啸。
background.en: A giant megathrust earthquake of about magnitude 9.1–9.3 struck off northwestern Sumatra and generated a tsunami across the Indian Ocean.

course.zh: 海啸在数小时内袭击印度尼西亚、斯里兰卡、印度、泰国、马尔代夫和东非。缺乏预警系统与公众教育放大了伤亡。
course.en: The waves struck Indonesia, Sri Lanka, India, Thailand, the Maldives and East Africa within hours. The absence of warning systems and public education magnified the toll.

outcome.zh: 约22.7万人死亡或失踪，是近代史上最严重的海啸灾难之一。灾后印度洋海啸预警系统逐步建立。
outcome.en: About 227,000 people died or went missing, one of the deadliest tsunamis in modern history. An Indian Ocean warning system was built after the disaster.

summary.zh: 日本投降后，苏加诺与哈达在雅加达宣读《独立宣言》，宣布荷属东印度独立为印度尼西亚共和国，随后展开四年多的独立战争。
summary.en: After Japan's surrender, Sukarno and Hatta read the Proclamation of Independence in Jakarta, declaring the Dutch East Indies the Republic of Indonesia and opening more than four years of independence war.

background.zh: 荷兰殖民统治在1942年被日本占领取代。日本为动员资源而扶植印尼民族主义领袖，同时其占领也摧毁了荷兰殖民机器的权威。
background.en: Dutch colonial rule was replaced by Japanese occupation in 1942. Japan cultivated Indonesian nationalist leaders to mobilize resources, while the occupation destroyed the authority of the Dutch colonial state.

course.zh: 1945年8月日本投降后，苏加诺与哈达在学生团体压力下于8月17日在雅加达住所前宣读简短宣言。随后制定宪法、成立政府，但荷兰拒绝承认并发动“警察行动”。
course.en: After Japan's surrender in August 1945, Sukarno and Hatta, pressed by student groups, read a short proclamation outside Sukarno's Jakarta house on 17 August. A constitution and government followed, but the Dutch refused recognition and launched 'police actions'.

outcome.zh: 经联合国斡旋与武装抵抗，荷兰在1949年海牙圆桌会议后移交主权。独立战争造成大量伤亡，也留下西巴布亚等未决问题。
outcome.en: After UN mediation and armed resistance, the Dutch transferred sovereignty following the 1949 Hague Round Table. The war caused heavy casualties and left unresolved questions such as West Papua.

why.zh: 印尼独立是二战后去殖民化浪潮的早期案例，说明日本占领、民族主义动员与冷战外交如何共同塑造一个新国家。
why.en: Indonesian independence is an early case of post-war decolonization, showing how Japanese occupation, nationalist mobilization and Cold War diplomacy together shaped a new state.

actors.zh: 维托里奥·埃马努埃莱二世

summary.zh: 在加富尔的外交、加里波第的远征与马志尼的民族主义推动下，意大利诸邦于1861年统一为意大利王国，1870年并入罗马。
summary.en: Through Cavour's diplomacy, Garibaldi's expeditions and Mazzini's nationalism, the Italian states unified as the Kingdom of Italy in 1861, with Rome added in 1870.

background.zh: 1815年维也纳体系把意大利分割为奥地利控制的北部、教皇国与两西西里王国等。拿破仑时期的改革已唤醒中产阶级的民族意识，烧炭党与青年意大利组织持续鼓动统一。
background.en: The 1815 Vienna settlement divided Italy into Austrian-controlled northern states, the Papal States and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. Napoleonic reforms had awakened a middle-class national consciousness, and Carbonari and Young Italy kept agitation alive.

course.zh: 1859年撒丁王国与法国联手击败奥地利，夺取伦巴第。1860年加里波第率“千人远征”征服西西里与那不勒斯，随后把南方交给维托里奥·埃马努埃莱二世。1861年意大利王国宣告成立。
course.en: In 1859 Sardinia and France defeated Austria and took Lombardy. In 1860 Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand conquered Sicily and Naples, then handed the south to Victor Emmanuel II. The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in 1861.

outcome.zh: 威尼托在1866年、罗马在1870年并入王国。统一以皮埃蒙特君主制为中心，地方差异、南北差距与教皇关系成为长期问题。
outcome.en: Venetia joined in 1866 and Rome in 1870. Unification centred on the Piedmontese monarchy, leaving regional differences, the north–south divide and relations with the papacy as long-term problems.

why.zh: 意大利统一说明民族国家既可由战争与外交自上而下建立，也可由志愿军与大众动员自下而上推动；两者最终都服从于君主制妥协。
why.en: Italian unification shows a nation-state built both from above by war and diplomacy and from below by volunteers and mass mobilization — with both ultimately subordinated to a monarchical compromise.

background.zh: 广岛、长崎核爆与苏联参战后，日本最高战争指导会议出现分裂。8月14日，天皇在御前会议上决定接受《波茨坦公告》。
background.en: After the atomic bombings and Soviet entry, Japan's supreme war council was divided. On 14 August the Emperor decided at an imperial conference to accept the Potsdam Declaration.

course.zh: 8月15日中午，天皇通过广播发表《终战诏书》，宣布接受《波茨坦公告》。诏书未直接使用“投降”一词，但实际结束了日本的战争。
course.en: At noon on 15 August the Emperor broadcast the Imperial Rescript on the Termination of the War, accepting the Potsdam Declaration. The rescript did not use the word 'surrender' directly, but ended Japan's war.

outcome.zh: 各地日军陆续停止战斗，但正式投降须待9月2日签署投降书。8月15日成为中国、朝鲜半岛和东南亚多地纪念战争结束的日子。
outcome.en: Japanese forces began to cease fighting, though formal surrender awaited the instrument signed on 2 September. 15 August is commemorated as the end of the war in China, Korea and parts of Southeast Asia.

title.en: Japan Signs the Instrument of Surrender

place.zh: 东京湾 · 密苏里号战舰

background.zh: 8月15日天皇宣布接受《波茨坦公告》后，盟军与日本就正式投降仪式进行安排。麦克阿瑟被任命为盟军最高统帅。
background.en: After the Emperor's 15 August acceptance of the Potsdam Declaration, the Allies and Japan arranged the formal surrender. MacArthur was appointed Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers.

course.zh: 9月2日上午，日本外相重光葵和参谋总长梅津美治郎在东京湾密苏里号战舰上签署投降书，同盟国代表依次签字。
course.en: On the morning of 2 September, Foreign Minister Shigemitsu and General Umezu signed the instrument of surrender aboard USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, followed by Allied representatives.

outcome.zh: 投降书签署标志着第二次世界大战正式结束。日本进入盟军占领时期，直至1952年《旧金山和约》生效。
outcome.en: The signing formally ended World War II. Japan entered Allied occupation until the San Francisco Peace Treaty took effect in 1952.

title.zh: 日本投降 · 二战结束

place.zh: 东京湾 · 密苏里号战舰

background.zh: 1945年8月，日本在核爆、苏联参战和盟军封锁下决定接受《波茨坦公告》。
background.en: In August 1945, under atomic bombing, Soviet entry and Allied blockade, Japan decided to accept the Potsdam Declaration.

course.zh: 8月15日天皇广播宣布接受公告；9月2日日本代表在密苏里号战舰上签署投降书。
course.en: The Emperor announced acceptance on 15 August; on 2 September Japanese representatives signed the instrument of surrender aboard USS Missouri.

outcome.zh: 第二次世界大战正式结束，日本进入盟军占领时期，战后国际秩序开始形成。
outcome.en: World War II formally ended, Japan entered Allied occupation, and the postwar international order took shape.

background.zh: 二战结束后朝鲜半岛以北纬38度线分区占领，美苏各自支持政权，南北统一谈判失败。1950年6月朝鲜人民军南进。
background.en: After World War II Korea was divided at the 38th parallel under Soviet and American occupation, with rival regimes and failed unification talks. In June 1950 North Korean forces advanced south.

course.zh: 联合国军干涉后战局反复，1950年10月中国志愿军入朝。1951年后战线稳定在三八线附近，双方开始停战谈判。
course.en: UN forces intervened and the front swung back and forth; Chinese volunteers entered in October 1950. After 1951 the line stabilised near the 38th parallel and armistice talks began.

outcome.zh: 1953年签署停战协定，未签和平条约。半岛分裂固化，驻韩美军与东北亚安全格局延续至今。
outcome.en: An armistice was signed in 1953 without a peace treaty. The division hardened and the US military presence and Northeast Asian security order persist.

sources.label: Imperial War Museums — A short history of the Korean War

actors.zh: 胡安·塞巴斯蒂安·埃尔卡诺

summary.zh: 麦哲伦船队从西班牙向西航行，穿过南美海峡进入太平洋，最终由埃尔卡诺率维多利亚号返回，完成人类首次环球航行。
summary.en: Magellan's fleet sailed west from Spain, passed through the South American strait into the Pacific, and Elcano brought the Victoria home, completing the first circumnavigation of the globe.

background.zh: 《托德西利亚斯条约》把世界分给西葡两国，但香料群岛的归属不明。西班牙希望找到一条向西通往摩鹿加群岛的航线，以挑战葡萄牙的印度洋垄断。
background.en: Tordesillas divided the world between Spain and Portugal, but the ownership of the Spice Islands was unclear. Spain sought a westward route to the Moluccas to challenge Portugal's Indian Ocean monopoly.

course.zh: 1519年9月船队从桑卢卡尔出发，沿南美海岸南下，1520年10月穿过麦哲伦海峡进入太平洋。横渡太平洋期间补给几乎耗尽，1521年麦哲伦在菲律宾麦克坦岛被杀。
course.en: The fleet left Sanlúcar in September 1519, followed the South American coast and in October 1520 passed the strait into the Pacific. Supplies ran out during the crossing; Magellan was killed on Mactan in the Philippines in 1521.

outcome.zh: 维多利亚号经印度洋绕过好望角，1522年9月返回西班牙，18名幸存者完成航行。航行证明地球可以被环绕，也暴露了纬度和经度测量的巨大误差。
outcome.en: The Victoria crossed the Indian Ocean and rounded the Cape, returning in September 1522 with eighteen survivors. The voyage proved the globe could be circumnavigated and exposed huge errors in longitude measurement.

why.zh: 首次环球航行把大西洋、太平洋与印度洋连成一个可被单一船队穿越的空间，是全球化的早期物质证明。
why.en: The first circumnavigation joined the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Oceans into a space a single fleet could cross — an early material proof of globalization.

background.zh: 约翰王在对法战争、征税与教会冲突中失去贵族支持。男爵们以武力迫使国王承认一系列权利与惯例。
background.en: King John lost baronial support through war with France, taxation and conflict with the Church. The barons used force to make him accept a series of rights and customs.

course.zh: 1215年6月，约翰王在兰尼米德签署《大宪章》，限制王权征税、任意拘押和没收财产。教宗随后宣布无效，但后世多次重颁。
course.en: In June 1215 John sealed Magna Carta at Runnymede, limiting arbitrary taxation, imprisonment and seizure of property. The Pope annulled it, but later kings reissued it.

outcome.zh: 《大宪章》成为英美宪政传统的重要象征，尤其“未经同侪合法审判不得剥夺自由”的条款影响深远；其原始文本主要保护贵族，而非普遍人权。
outcome.en: Magna Carta became a symbol of the English and American constitutional tradition, especially the clause on judgment by peers; its original text mainly protected barons, not universal rights.

summary.zh: 松迪亚塔在13世纪建立马里帝国，控制跨撒哈拉黄金与盐贸易；曼萨·穆萨1324年的朝觐使马里的财富与伊斯兰学术中心廷巴克图闻名于世。
summary.en: Sundiata founded the Mali Empire in the thirteenth century, controlling trans-Saharan gold and salt trade; Mansa Musa's 1324 pilgrimage made Mali's wealth and the scholarly centre of Timbuktu famous.

background.zh: 加纳帝国衰落后，尼日尔河上游的曼丁哥诸部崛起。松迪亚塔在1235年前后击败苏苏首领苏曼古鲁，整合曼丁哥联盟。
background.en: After Ghana's decline, Mandinka chiefdoms on the upper Niger rose. Around 1235 Sundiata defeated the Susu leader Sumanguru and consolidated the Mandinka alliance.

course.zh: 马里以尼亚尼为中心，控制金矿、盐路与尼日尔河贸易。曼萨·穆萨在位时帝国达到鼎盛，他1324年经开罗前往麦加，随行携带大量黄金，导致当地金价长期下跌。
course.en: Centred on Niani, Mali controlled goldfields, salt routes and Niger trade. Under Mansa Musa the empire reached its height; his 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca via Cairo, with vast quantities of gold, depressed Egyptian gold prices for years.

outcome.zh: 穆萨延请学者与建筑师到廷巴克图，桑科雷清真寺与大学使该城成为西非伊斯兰学术中心。帝国在15世纪后因继承争端与桑海崛起而衰落。
outcome.en: Musa brought scholars and architects to Timbuktu, where the Sankore mosque and university made the city a West African centre of Islamic learning. After the fifteenth century, succession disputes and the rise of Songhai eroded Mali.

why.zh: 马里帝国提醒我们，中世纪非洲的财富与学术并非边缘现象，而是跨撒哈拉世界体系的核心部分。
why.en: Mali is a reminder that medieval African wealth and scholarship were not marginal but central to the trans-Saharan world system.

title.zh: 毛利人抵达奥特亚罗瓦

summary.zh: 波利尼西亚航海者依靠星辰、洋流与候鸟知识，在13世纪前后抵达新西兰，成为毛利人的祖先，并发展出独特的村落、园艺与战舞文化。
summary.en: Using stars, currents and bird movements, Polynesian voyagers reached New Zealand around the thirteenth century, becoming the ancestors of the Māori and developing distinctive settlements, horticulture and warrior culture.

background.zh: 波利尼西亚人自公元前一千纪起向东太平洋扩散，形成地球上最广阔的航海文明。新西兰是最后被人类定居的大块陆地之一。
background.en: From the first millennium BCE Polynesians spread across the eastern Pacific, creating the widest-ranging voyaging civilization on Earth. New Zealand was among the last large landmasses settled by humans.

course.zh: 传统讲述独木舟船队从哈瓦基（常与塔希提一带联系）驶来，载着食物、作物与动物。考古显示早期聚落集中在沿海与河口，以恐鸟、海兽和园艺为生。
course.en: Traditions tell of canoe fleets sailing from Hawaiki, often linked to the Tahiti region, carrying food, plants and animals. Archaeology places early settlements on coasts and river mouths, where people hunted moa, fished and gardened.

outcome.zh: 毛利社会以部落（iwi）、次部落（hapū）与家族为单位，形成“kāinga”聚落与“marae”礼仪空间。1840年《怀唐伊条约》后，殖民扩张与土地战争深刻改变了毛利社会。
outcome.en: Māori society organized around iwi, hapū and whānau, with kāinga settlements and marae ceremonial spaces. After the 1840 Treaty of Waitangi, colonial expansion and land wars transformed Māori society.

why.zh: 毛利抵达是波利尼西亚航海技术的顶峰，也提醒我们太平洋历史并非欧洲探险的空白前奏。
why.en: The Māori arrival marks the peak of Polynesian navigation and reminds us that Pacific history is not a blank prelude to European exploration.

place.zh: 中国北平西南 · 卢沟桥
place.en: Marco Polo Bridge, southwest of Beiping, China

background.zh: 1931年九一八事变后，日本控制中国东北并不断向华北渗透。1937年7月7日夜，日军在卢沟桥附近演习，以一名士兵失踪为由要求进入宛平城搜查。
background.en: After the Mukden Incident of 1931, Japan controlled Manchuria and pressed into northern China. On the night of 7 July 1937, Japanese troops on exercise near the Marco Polo Bridge demanded entry to Wanping to search for a missing soldier.

course.zh: 中国守军拒绝日军进城，双方交火。事变后日军不断增兵，7月底攻占北平、天津；中国方面由第29军局部抵抗转向全国动员。
course.en: Chinese defenders refused entry and fighting broke out. Japan reinforced and took Beiping and Tianjin by late July, while China moved from local resistance by the 29th Army to national mobilisation.

outcome.zh: 卢沟桥事变成为全民族抗战的起点；国共两党走向合作，抗日民族统一战线形成。它也被视为第二次世界大战亚洲战场的开端之一。
outcome.en: The incident became the starting point of China's full-scale War of Resistance; the KMT and CCP moved toward cooperation and a united front. It is also widely treated as the opening of World War II in Asia.

summary.zh: 旃陀罗笈多在前321年前后建立孔雀王朝，首次统一印度大部；阿育王在羯陵伽战争后转向佛法治国，留下石柱与摩崖敕令。
summary.en: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE, unifying most of India for the first time; after the Kalinga war Ashoka turned to rule by dharma, leaving rock and pillar edicts.

background.zh: 亚历山大东征后，印度西北部出现权力真空。旃陀罗笈多借助地方力量推翻难陀王朝，并与塞琉古帝国达成边界安排。
background.en: Alexander's campaigns left a power vacuum in northwestern India. Chandragupta overthrew the Nanda dynasty with local support and reached a frontier settlement with the Seleucid empire.

course.zh: 孔雀王朝以华氏城为中心，建立四省制、道路与税收体系。阿育王在即位第八年征服羯陵伽，战争造成大量伤亡；据其敕令，他随后皈依佛教，倡导宽容、公共福利与非暴力。
course.en: Centred on Pataliputra, the empire developed provincial administration, roads and taxation. In his eighth year Ashoka conquered Kalinga at great cost; according to his edicts he then embraced Buddhism and promoted tolerance, public welfare and nonviolence.

outcome.zh: 帝国在阿育王死后迅速分裂，前185年为巽伽王朝取代。阿育王的狮子柱头后来成为印度共和国国徽，其“法”观念持续影响南亚政治。
outcome.en: The empire fragmented after Ashoka and was replaced by the Shunga dynasty in 185 BCE. Ashoka's lion capital later became the emblem of the Republic of India, and his idea of dharma continued to shape South Asian politics.

why.zh: 孔雀王朝是南亚次大陆“帝国统一”的原型；阿育王则提供了以公共伦理而非单纯武力统治的早期范本。
why.en: The Maurya empire is South Asia's archetype of subcontinental unity, and Ashoka an early model of rule through public ethics rather than conquest alone.

sources.label: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi

background.zh: 黑船来航后日本被迫开国，幕府权威下降。西南诸藩志士以“尊王攘夷”为号召，推动倒幕。
background.en: After Perry's arrival Japan was forced to open, weakening the shogunate. Activists from southwestern domains used the slogan “revere the Emperor, expel the barbarians” to push for its overthrow.

course.zh: 1868年1月，明治天皇发布王政复古大号令，德川庆喜败退。新政府随后推行废藩置县、征兵制、地税改革、殖产兴业和文明开化。
course.en: In January 1868 the Meiji Emperor proclaimed the restoration of imperial rule and Tokugawa Yoshinobu was defeated. The new government abolished domains, introduced conscription, land-tax reform, industrialisation and Western learning.

outcome.zh: 日本迅速建立中央集权与工业基础，成为亚洲首个工业化强国；改革也带来社会紧张、对外扩张与军国主义道路。
outcome.en: Japan rapidly built a centralised state and industrial base, becoming Asia's first industrial power; the changes also brought social tension, overseas expansion and militarism.

background.zh: 墨西哥城建于古湖床之上，松软的湖积土会放大地震波。20世纪后期城市人口与高层建筑快速增长，抗震规范与应急体系尚未充分成熟。
background.en: Mexico City is built on a former lakebed whose soft sediments amplify seismic waves. Rapid late-20th-century population and high-rise growth outpaced building codes and emergency systems.

course.zh: 1985年9月19日上午，墨西哥太平洋沿岸发生8.0级地震，墨西哥城大量中高层建筑倒塌，医院、学校与政府大楼受损。市民自发组成救援队，在废墟中搜寻幸存者；余震与救援持续数日。
course.en: On the morning of 19 September 1985 an magnitude 8.0 earthquake struck off Mexico's Pacific coast, collapsing many mid- and high-rise buildings in Mexico City and damaging hospitals, schools and government offices. Citizens formed rescue brigades to search the rubble, and aftershocks and rescue work continued for days.

outcome.zh: 死亡人数估计从数千到一万以上不等，数十万人无家可归。灾后墨西哥修订建筑规范、建立民防体系，并把9月19日作为全国防灾演练日；这场地震也成为拉美城市灾难记忆与公民动员的重要象征。
outcome.en: Death-toll estimates range from several thousand to over 10,000, with hundreds of thousands left homeless. Mexico revised building codes, built a civil-protection system and turned 19 September into a national drill day; the earthquake became a symbol of urban disaster memory and civic mobilisation in Latin America.

summary.zh: 旭烈兀率蒙古军攻陷巴格达，处死末代阿拔斯哈里发，焚掠城市并摧毁图书馆；延续五百年的阿拔斯哈里发制度就此终结。
summary.en: Hulagu's Mongol army took Baghdad, executed the last Abbasid caliph, burned and plundered the city and destroyed its libraries, ending five centuries of Abbasid caliphate.

background.zh: 阿拔斯王朝自945年起受白益王朝与塞尔柱人控制，哈里发多为象征性领袖。13世纪蒙古西征摧毁花剌子模后，旭烈兀受命肃清伊斯兰世界东部。
background.en: Since 945 the Abbasids had been dominated by the Buyids and then the Seljuks, with the caliph largely symbolic. After destroying Khwarazm, Hulagu was ordered to subdue the eastern Islamic world.

course.zh: 1258年1月蒙古军围城，利用底格里斯河两岸的攻城器械突破防御。哈里发投降后与王室成员被处死，城市遭大规模屠杀、焚毁与劫掠，智慧宫等藏书损失惨重。
course.en: The Mongols besieged the city in January 1258 and broke its defences with siege engines on both banks of the Tigris. The caliph surrendered and was executed with members of his house; the city was massacred, burned and looted, with heavy losses to libraries such as the House of Wisdom.

outcome.zh: 巴格达降为蒙古伊儿汗国的地方城市，伊斯兰世界的政治中心转向开罗与后来的奥斯曼。蒙古人在1260年艾因贾鲁特战败后停止西进。
outcome.en: Baghdad became a provincial city of the Mongol Ilkhanate, and the political centre of the Islamic world shifted to Cairo and later the Ottomans. Mongol expansion westward stopped after defeat at Ain Jalut in 1260.

why.zh: 巴格达之陷是蒙古征服破坏性的象征，也说明一个依赖象征性哈里发的政治体系在军事危机中多么脆弱。
why.en: The sack is a symbol of Mongol destructiveness and shows how fragile a political order resting on a symbolic caliphate could be in a military crisis.

title.zh: 蒙特阿尔班与萨波特克

place.zh: 墨西哥瓦哈卡谷地 · 蒙特阿尔班

background.zh: 瓦哈卡谷地由多个农耕聚落组成。约公元前500年，萨波特克人在谷地中央的山顶营建大型仪式与行政中心，整合周边人口。
background.en: The Oaxaca Valley was home to several farming communities. Around 500 BCE the Zapotec built a large ceremonial and administrative centre on a hilltop at the centre of the valley, integrating the surrounding population.

course.zh: 蒙特阿尔班拥有规划过的广场、神庙、球场与宫殿，山坡上修建梯田与住宅。萨波特克人发展出历法、象形文字与黑陶传统，城市在全盛期可能居住两万余人。
course.en: Monte Albán had a planned plaza, temples, a ball court and palaces, with terraces and residences on the slopes. The Zapotec developed a calendar, hieroglyphic writing and black pottery; the city may have housed more than 20,000 people at its height.

outcome.zh: 城市在公元8世纪前后逐渐衰落，但蒙特阿尔班长期被后世米斯特克人继续使用。1987年列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产，是理解前哥伦布美洲城市文明的关键遗址。
outcome.en: The city declined around the 8th century CE, though later Mixtec groups continued to use the site. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987 and is a key site for understanding pre-Columbian urban civilisation.

summary.zh: 日本关东军炸毁南满铁路并嫁祸中国军队，随即占领沈阳与东北。事变成为日本侵华与二战亚洲战场的起点之一。
summary.en: Japan's Kwantung Army blew up the South Manchurian Railway, blamed Chinese troops and seized Shenyang and Manchuria. The incident became a starting point of Japan's invasion of China and the Asian theatre of World War II.

background.zh: 日本在东北拥有南满铁路与关东军驻屯权，长期寻求扩大势力。1931年世界经济危机与日本国内政治右转，使军方冒险行动更易获得支持。
background.en: Japan held the South Manchurian Railway and garrison rights in Manchuria and had long sought greater control. The 1931 Depression and a rightward shift in Japanese politics made military adventurism easier to sustain.

course.zh: 9月18日夜，关东军在柳条湖附近炸毁铁路，诬称中国军队所为，进攻北大营。张学良执行不抵抗政策，日军在数月内占领东北三省，1932年扶植伪满洲国。
course.en: On the night of 18 September the Kwantung Army blew up track near Liutiaohu, blamed Chinese troops and attacked Beidaying. Zhang Xueliang followed a non-resistance policy; within months Japan held the three northeastern provinces and in 1932 created the puppet state of Manchukuo.

outcome.zh: 国际联盟派李顿调查团，认定日本为侵略者，但未能制止。日本退出国联，继续扩张；中国向国联申诉的外交路线受挫。
outcome.en: The League of Nations sent the Lytton Commission, which found Japan the aggressor but could not stop it. Japan left the League and continued expanding; China's strategy of appealing to the League was disappointed.

why.zh: 九一八事变暴露了集体安全机制的无力，也说明局部军事冒险如何在没有正式宣战的情况下改变一个大陆的秩序。
why.en: Mukden exposed the weakness of collective security and showed how a local military adventure could reshape a continent without a formal declaration of war.

background.zh: 2000年代以来，南亚城市恐怖袭击频发。孟买是印度金融与媒体中心，火车站、酒店与宗教场所人流密集，安全防护面临挑战。
background.en: South Asia saw repeated urban terrorist attacks from the 2000s. Mumbai, India's financial and media centre, concentrates railway stations, hotels and religious sites, making protection difficult.

course.zh: 2008年11月26日晚，十名武装分子乘船抵达孟买，袭击贾特拉帕蒂·希瓦吉火车站、泰姬陵酒店、奥贝罗伊酒店与纳里曼大楼等目标。印度国家安全卫队展开约60小时清剿，事件于29日结束。
course.en: On the evening of 26 November 2008, ten attackers arrived in Mumbai by boat and struck Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, the Taj and Oberoi hotels, Nariman House and other targets. India's National Security Guard mounted a roughly 60-hour operation that ended on 29 November.

outcome.zh: 袭击造成166人死亡、300余人受伤。印度指责巴基斯坦境内的武装组织策划袭击，南亚关系一度紧张；印度随后加强海岸安全、城市警务与反恐协调。孟买以纪念碑与年度悼念铭记遇难者。
outcome.en: The attacks killed 166 people and injured more than 300. India blamed a Pakistan-based militant group, sharply raising regional tensions; India subsequently strengthened coastal security, urban policing and counter-terrorism coordination. Mumbai commemorates the victims with memorials and annual observances.

background.zh: 广岛核爆后日本仍未投降。8月8日苏联对日宣战并于9日进军中国东北。美国计划第二次核打击，首要目标是小仓，长崎为备选。
background.en: Japan still did not surrender after Hiroshima. On 8 August the Soviet Union declared war and invaded Manchuria on 9 August. The United States planned a second strike, with Kokura as the primary target and Nagasaki as the alternative.

course.zh: 8月9日，B-29“博克斯卡”因小仓上空云层厚重改飞长崎，投下代号“胖子”的钚弹，在城市上空爆炸。长崎地形多山，爆心位于浦上河谷。
course.en: On 9 August the B-29 Bockscar diverted to Nagasaki because of clouds over Kokura and dropped the plutonium bomb 'Fat Man'. The hilly terrain confined the blast to the Urakami valley.

outcome.zh: 到1945年底，死亡人数估计约3.5万至7万。日本最高战争指导会议在核爆与苏联参战的双重压力下转向接受《波茨坦公告》。
outcome.en: By the end of 1945 the death toll is estimated at roughly 35,000–70,000. Under the combined shock of the bombings and Soviet entry, Japan's supreme war council moved to accept the Potsdam Declaration.

sources.label: U.S. National Archives — Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Britannica — Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

actors.en: Nanjing civilians and prisoners of war

background.zh: 淞沪会战结束后，日军向中国首都南京推进。中国军队在装备与补给劣势下撤退，大量平民滞留城内。
background.en: After the Battle of Shanghai, Japanese forces advanced on Nanjing, China's capital. Chinese troops withdrew under severe equipment and supply disadvantages, leaving large civilian populations in the city.

course.zh: 1937年12月13日南京陷落后，日军在数周内对平民和战俘实施大规模屠杀、强奸、纵火与劫掠。留在城内的国际人士建立“南京安全区”，留下了日记、影像与证词。
course.en: After Nanjing fell on 13 December 1937, Japanese forces carried out mass killings, rape, arson and looting against civilians and prisoners over several weeks. International residents established the Nanjing Safety Zone and left diaries, photographs and testimony.

outcome.zh: 死亡人数长期存在不同估计，从数万到三十万以上；远东国际军事法庭与南京军事法庭均认定发生了大规模暴行。南京大屠杀成为中国与东亚战争记忆的核心事件，也是当代历史争议的焦点之一。
outcome.en: Death-toll estimates have long varied from tens of thousands to over 300,000; the International Military Tribunal for the Far East and the Nanjing War Crimes Tribunal both found that large-scale atrocities occurred. The massacre remains central to Chinese and East Asian war memory and to contemporary historical disputes.

sources.label: Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre — official English site

background.zh: 英国为平衡茶叶贸易向中国大量输入鸦片，清政府禁烟。1839年林则徐在虎门销烟，英国以武力回应。
background.en: Britain exported large quantities of opium to China to balance the tea trade, and the Qing moved to suppress it. In 1839 Lin Zexu destroyed opium at Humen; Britain responded with force.

course.zh: 英军攻占沿海城市并沿长江推进，1842年清廷被迫签订《南京条约》，割让香港岛、开放五口、赔款并协定关税。
course.en: British forces seized coastal cities and advanced up the Yangtze; in 1842 the Qing signed the Treaty of Nanking, ceding Hong Kong Island, opening five ports, paying an indemnity and accepting tariff terms.

outcome.zh: 中国被迫纳入不平等条约体系，主权与关税受损；战争也成为中国近代民族主义与改革运动的起点。
